result.title: Mean Accuracy Is the Wrong Estimand for a Release Decision
result.summary: A release decision about a fine-tuned model is an operational commitment about the \emph{next} rerun of its training recipe. Yet standard benchmark reporting gives only the mean accuracy of past seeds. These target fundamentally different questions: release decisions depend on catastrophic tail risk, whereas standard evaluation reports only central tendency. Because fine-tuning induces bimodal mode collapse, high average accuracy frequently conceals severe failure rates. Auditing $2\,124$ fine-tuned models across eleven language models, we show that shipping models based on mean accuracy violates a $10\%$ deployment failure budget $48.0\%$ of the time. Common heuristics like $\bar b - 2σ$ prove equally dangerous: by underestimating variance on small samples, they become most permissive when evidence is weakest. We introduce \textbf{recipe cards}, an evaluation framework that directly certifies rerun tail failure rates using exact finite-sample binomial bounds. Recipe cards reduce held-out budget violations to $0.6\%$, enforce a mathematical sample floor ($N \ge 22$) that prevents certification on thin evidence, and explicitly refuse unverified claims under domain and task shifts.

AI.brief_summary: 论文论证平均准确率不适合作为模型发布依据，因微调会引发双峰模式坍缩、尾部失败被均值掩盖；作者审计 2124 个微调模型并提出 recipe cards，用精确有限样本二项界认证重跑尾部失败率，并设最低样本量门槛、在域与任务迁移时拒绝未验证主张。
AI.relevance_reason: 与研究中的评价环节可能相关：latent 推理方法的收益常以少数种子的均值汇报，这一统计认证思路可供核查如何评估跨种子鲁棒性、失败尾部与样本量下限。
